newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent has room for upside in short term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent has room for upside in short term.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+Brent still has some life left in it and yesterday's gains have set the stage for a further upwards move. Support is at around $18.04 today.
+But the positive action is likely to prove to be a short term bounce and in the longer term prices are set to head downwards for a test of last month's $17.32 low.
IPE Brent crude oil futures appear to be in "corrective bounce mode" and this is likely to continue today - with important support at around $18.05 a barrel.
But the bears are lurking and technical analysts expect this year's downwards progression to resume shortly.
August Brent crude oil closed 13 cents a barrel firmer on Monday at $18.19 a barrel while July gas oil, which expires on Thursday, was 75 cents a tonne down at $161.25.
Dealers expect early gains in gas oil futures as the market catches up with Brent's late rise on Monday.

Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS in the U.K. said in a report released early on Monday that the market remained above a key supportive trendline on the spot month continuation chart, running from the $17.32 lows to the $17.70 lows of June 25.
He said trend support crossed the price action at $17.98 on Monday (in fact the market reached a low of $17.97). The line continues through $18.04 on Tuesday, $18.04 on Wednesday, and so on, he said.
"While the price is north of the line the rebuild that started last month looks intact. A settlement below the line and $17.49 and $17.32 are realistic downside targets."
Tom James at Credit Lyonnais in Singapore pegged support at $18.02 and trendline resistance at $18.31. "I am cautiously a seller of Brent at the moment," he said.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International in the U.S. said: "Stay bearish within the context of additional corrective strength in the morning to above $18.28."

"This bounce from Monday's $17.97 low is corrective and appears capable of at least slightly breaching $18.28 on Tuesday. This corrective rise ought to wane over the coming day or so, and if needed, strong resistance is thought to reside around $18.58ish."

Sceats also said that above that level a key number is $18.96 - this is not only the 50 percent retracement on the spot continuation chart of the move from the $20.60 high on May 16 and the $17.32 low on June 11, but also the high point of the latest up move, reached on July 2.
James said gas oil was supported at $160 while resistance would weigh in at $161.75 and then $164.25.
"I am still bearish this market, however today the market is expected to find it difficult to move lower with short term mathematical indicators looking oversold.
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
